audit.title: Data Quality, Responsibility & Trust Model
audit.summary: This is a clean, well-structured conceptual page explaining DataLink's single-source trust model, anchored by a strong comparison table that clearly separates Chainlink's role from the Data Provider's. Its biggest GEO strength is that table — a highly liftable, reason-bearing structure engines can quote directly. Its biggest opportunities are the total absence of machine-readable metadata (no JSON-LD, canonical, or dates) and thin citation/specificity, both of which cap retrieval and trust. Honest verdict: a solid page held back by missing schema and by concept-titled (rather than symptom-titled) headings that miss how developers actually query trust/liability questions.

recommendations.title: Add TechArticle JSON-LD + canonical + dates
recommendations.issue: "canonical: MISSING · datePublished absent / dateModified absent · JSON-LD: 0 blocks"
recommendations.change: Emit `TechArticle` JSON-LD with `headline`, `dateModified`, `about: "DataLink"`, and a self-referential `canonical`; surface a visible "Last updated" line.
recommendations.why: Freshness + schema are direct E-E-A-T/trust signals; their absence suppresses retrieval and citation confidence.

recommendations.title: Add symptom/liability-phrased headings
recommendations.issue: headings are concept-titled ("Single-Source Data vs. Aggregated Data") and miss liability queries
recommendations.change: Add sections titled "Who is responsible if a DataLink feed goes down?" and "Is Chainlink liable for DataLink data quality?" answered in the first sentence.
recommendations.why: Devs/legal reviewers query by question; question-phrased headings win retrieval that concept prose loses.

recommendations.title: Lead sections with the canonical claim, not the caveat
recommendations.issue: "While DataLink leverages the same underlying Chainlink Data Streams infrastructure…"
recommendations.change: Open with "For single-source DataLink feeds, the Data Provider — not Chainlink — is solely responsible for data quality," then give the transport caveat.
recommendations.why: The liftable first sentence should carry the core fact so skimmed/RAG chunks stand alone.

recommendations.title: Add concrete specifics on failure behavior
recommendations.where: "Data Sources" table cell / Risk Management list
recommendations.issue: "if the Data Provider experiences an outage, data flow for that specific feed ceases" — no quantification
recommendations.change: State what a consumer contract observes on outage (e.g., stale timestamp / no new reports), and quantify redundancy ("single source = 0 provider-level redundancy").
recommendations.why: Quantified, unit-bearing claims are among the highest-lift changes; replaces vague "most/robust."

recommendations.title: Add authoritative inline links
recommendations.issue: 0 external links; disclaimer and transport claims unattributed
recommendations.change: Link "report signing"/"secure transport" to the Data Streams architecture page and the "as is / as available" language to the canonical Chainlink terms page.
recommendations.why: Attributable claims raise citation rate and credibility.

recommendations.title: Define "single-source feed" verbatim near first use
recommendations.issue: term used before a crisp definition
recommendations.change: Add "A single-source DataLink feed delivers data from exactly one provider, with no cross-source aggregation or outlier detection by Chainlink."
recommendations.why: A self-contained definition is easy to lift verbatim into answers.

antiPatterns: Vague quantifiers "most" and "robust" (measured) — replace "most DataLink feeds" with a concrete share if known.
Stale/undated content: no visible or structured last-updated date.
No unresolved cross-references, no keyword stuffing, no marketing fluff detected.
offPageNotes: `llms.txt` is already referenced at the top of the page — good site-level signal; ensure this URL is listed in it.
Site-level: confirm `TechArticle`/`BreadcrumbList` schema is templated across `docs.chain.link`, since this page inherited none.
The CLI should pass raw `<head>` on future runs — head metadata could not be verified here, so schema/canonical findings rest on the served-HTML measurement.
